newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Howard says won't bow to threats on Dalai Lama.
newsitem.headline: Howard says won't bow to threats on Dalai Lama.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard, who has angered China by agreeing to meet the Dalai Lama of Tibet on Thursday, said on Wednesday he would not bow to threats of trade retaliation from foreign governments.
"I hope they don't carry through with that threat but I don't bow to threats," Howard said in a television interview due to be aired on Wednesday evening.
"No self-respecting prime minister of this country would ever bow to that kind of threat," Howard added.

China, which regards the Dalai Lama as a pro-independence campaigner bent on splitting China, on Tuesday threatened unspecified trade retaliation after news that Howard would receive the Tibetan god-king in his Sydney office on Thursday.
Howard told Channel Nine television that Beijing had "created a problem out of nothing" -- he had no choice but to meet the Dalai Lama.
He added that he did not expect the meeting to sour the strong trade and political relations between Australia and China.
